Prime Minister Narendra Modi has stressed the need to protect countries' banking system
from cyberterrorism, warning that modern wars are being fought not only through conventional
means but also by targeting economies.
Mr Modi was speaking after inaugurating the Reserve Bank of India's Data Center and
Cyber Security Training Institute at Jatney near Bhuvaneshwar Odisha this evening.
He said the new facilities will help protect countries' banking system against emerging
cyber threats.
Mr. Modi said India's banking sector has emerged as one of the most efficient in the
world with people having access to banking services around the clock.
Mr. Modi said development means balanced growth across India, creating opportunities

The deep depression over the Birbengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm by tomorrow
morning and further strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing the
Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday.
The India Meteorological Department IMD has forecast very heavy rainfall in Odisha and
Andhra Pradesh from Tuesday to Thursday in view of the approaching weather system.
Odisha and Andhra Pradesh have stepped up their preparedness measures to deal with the
potential impact of the developing cyclone.
The Odisha government has mobilized disaster response teams and stepped up precautionary
measures.
Our correspondent has the details.
The system is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla
and Bishakapatnam by the Wednesday 4 noon, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 115-125
km per hour and gusts reaching 140 km per hour.
Ganjam, Gajapati, Rai Gada, Korapu, Tanmalkangiri are among the districts facing high-tend risks,
with a red warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall on Wednesday.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Maaji has directed the administration to ensure preparedness
and minimize casualties.
Around 60 odd draft teams and 17 NDRF teams have been deployed, while 225 fire
services teams remain on high alert.
Kohl's colleges and Anganwadi centres in the five southern districts will remain closed
on Wednesday and Thursday.
Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea, while authorities are preparing
for evacuations and possible disruption to transport power supply and agricultural activities.
